upstream_fix_review.details: 3a10af93 only moves the baseval assignment (dgraph_fold.c:196); it does not change the error agreement. With it, the base-1 runs no longer abort with 'free(): invalid pointer' but all receiver and sender allocation failures still hang the other processes in release builds (verified: nth=3..6 base 1 exit=124 HANG, see /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G18-dgraph-fold-redist/repro/DGR-02/pristine7018_base1.txt). 0e79c872 only fixes the routine name in a debug-only message of hdgraphFold2 (hdgraph_fold.c:894).
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our P3 (7.0.17 0003) makes the first agreement unconditional and adds a collective allocation gate before edge data is sent; it still applies (one conflict: the message renamed by 0e79c872, which our patch also renames and renumbers to (20)).

review_accuracy: Mechanism and lines accurate (7.0.17 lines are the 7.0.16 ones +0/+1). Its first fix (agree on allocation success before posting edge data) is the right one. Its second fix (complete every posted request at fail3) is insufficient alone: the senders' edge-data Isends have no matching receive on the failed receiver and cannot complete. 'receivers sit in MPI_Allreduce' holds only in SCOTCH_DEBUG_DGRAPH1 builds; in release builds the agreements are compiled out and peers hang in MPI_Waitany/Finalize.
first_pass_critique: Status, location and reproduction correct. Its preferred sketch has defects: (a) the gate is two separate MPI_Allreduce calls, one in the sender block and one in the receiver block, so a sender-receiver would call it twice and the others once (collective mismatch); (b) on gate failure it frees the folding data and jumps to fail4 but the compacted original arrays and *flddataptr are still leaked and the senders' Isend-error paths still skip all frees; (c) it keeps the debug-only agreement before dgraphBuild4 unchanged. Its option 2 (TAGOK/TAGBAD handshake) is rightly rejected, but also because dgraphBuild4 is itself collective among receivers. The dead second-pass attempt had the right structure; I audited it against the maintainer's 7.0.17 idiom and kept it, adding the review of the threaded callers (dgraphFoldDup, kdgraphMapRbPart, hdgraphOrderNd duplicate the communicator, so the new Allreduces cannot cross between the two concurrent folds).

fix_options.label: A: collective allocation gate before edge data is sent, unconditional first agreement, one cleanup label (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Senders post only edge-count and vertex messages; pure receivers post their count/vertex receives, wait for the counts and allocate the edge array; then all processes agree (MPI_Allreduce MAX on orggrafptr->proccomm). On failure every pending communication is matched, so one MPI_Waitall over the whole (MPI_REQUEST_NULL-prefilled) request array drains them before buffers are freed. The first agreement (fail1) is always performed and also covers graph compaction and the debug parameter checks. All error paths share one cleanup label that frees the folding data, the communication array, the compacted arrays, the folded data array and the folded graph. The debug-only agreements before dgraphCheck and at the end are kept as designed (nothing but MPI calls can fail after the gate: dgraphBuild4 does not allocate). Same restructuring in hdgraphFold2().
fix_options.tested: Fault injection on every allocation of dgraphFold2 (receiver and sender, base 0/1, np=3,4) and of hdgraphFold2 (through dgraphOrderCompute): all processes return 1, no hang, no sanitizer report. After the series: check_strat_par, check_scotch_dgraph_{check,band,coarsen,order,grow,induce,redist}, check_libparmetis_{v3,dual}, check_prog_{dgord,dgpart,dgscat-dggath,dgtst} all exit 0 on the 32-bit ASan+UBSan tree and on the 64-bit Gnum tree ($WORK/chk_32_*.log, chk_64_*.log; the only sanitizer lines are pre-existing ones in library_dgraph_coarsen.c:163 and bgraph_bipart_ml.c:195, other groups); check_scotch_dgraph_{check,coarsen,order,redist,induce} and check_prog_dgord also pass on an ASan -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (chk_dbg_*.log). Zero compiler warnings in the three trees. git am of the 7 patches on a fresh clone of v7.0.17 succeeds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two small MPI_Allreduce per fold in release builds (one before posting, one before edge data), against a data exchange of half the graph: negligible. Reverses the maintainer's explicit choice to compile the first agreement out ('cannot be merged with a useful one'); there is no existing collective to piggyback on in release builds. Function grows by ~30 lines; six fail labels instead of four. MPI call failures (fatal by default) remain unrecoverable, as before.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Uses his 7.0.17 idiom exactly: 'cheklocval = 1; /* Assume an error */', goto failN, 'cheklocval = 0; /* Everything went well */' before the agreement label, a label inside the failure block that later code jumps back to (dgraphInduce2, 3c9b3ab: fail1 inside the memAllocGroup failure block), unconditional MPI_Allreduce at the fail label (hdgraphGather, 0635547).

fix_options.label: B: receiver-side cleanup only (drain own requests, free leaks), first agreement unconditional, no gate
fix_options.summary: At fail3 the receiver waits for its own posted requests, frees the folding data and the compacted arrays, then fails; the first agreement is made unconditional.
fix_options.tested: compiles (mpicc -c, 0 warnings); not run: by construction the senders' edge-data Isends stay unmatched
fix_options.tradeoffs: Fixes the use-after-free and the leaks of the receiver only; senders of edge data to the failed receiver still block forever in their final MPI_Waitall (large messages) and the other receivers return 0. Smallest diff.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Leaves the hang the review reports; he would not take a partial fix.

fix_options.label: C: over-allocate the receiver edge array before the first agreement, no second gate
fix_options.summary: Pure receivers allocate their edge array with an upper bound (remote edges, or received vertices times degrglbmax, plus local edges) before fail1, so that nothing but MPI calls can fail after the single agreement; the array is shrunk with memRealloc once the counts are known.
fix_options.tested: compiles (mpicc -c, 0 warnings); not run
fix_options.tradeoffs: One agreement instead of two, but the bound min(edgeglbnbr - edgelocnbr, vertrcvnbr * degrglbmax) can be much larger than the exact size (star-like graphs), which defeats the purpose of folding small graphs; relies on the shrinking memRealloc never failing.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He sized this array exactly on purpose (edge counts are exchanged first); extra peak memory in the fold is what the design avoids.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. The release-build agreement is the open maintainer decision (unconditional MPI_Allreduce in non-debug builds); upstream's 7.0.18 fixes for this review did not add any such agreement in these files.

our_title: User permutation to SCOTCH_dgraphRedist corrupts edges: in-place unpack assumes receive order
ran: repro/DGR-04/redistperm.c (MPI_Init_thread), pristine 7.0.18 ASan /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/infra18/asan: `mpirun -np 2 ./redistperm_asan 4 0 2` -> ERROR: AddressSanitizer: memcpy-param-overlap; `-np 2 ... 8 0 2`, `-np 3 ... 40 0 0`, `-np 4 ... 41 1 0` -> rc=0 then 'dgraphCheck: arc data do not match' (silently wrong graph). Patched (P1) 32-bit and 64-bit trees: all four rev=1 rc=0 check=0 bad-adjacency=0; check_scotch_dgraph_redist passes on both. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G18-dgraph-fold-redist/repro/DGR-04/redistperm_7018.txt
severity_note: Public API, documented usage (permgsttab 'must be valid' for local and ghost vertices, any order), release builds return 0 with a wrong graph; needs a receiver whose own send buffer is small (receives much more than it keeps), which is the normal use of a redistribution.
evidence: dgraph_redist.c:355: `MAX (dstedgelocdlt, srcgrafptr->degrglbmax)) * sizeof (Gnum)), /* TRICK: degrmax to avoid overlap */`; :433 `dstvlblloctax[dstvertlocnum] = drcvdatidx;    /* TRICK: record data position in label array  */`; :469 `memCpy (dstedgeloctax + dstedgelocnum, drcvdattab + drcvdatidx, dstdegrval * sizeof (Gnum)); /* TRICK: will never overlap */`
review_accuracy: Accurate, including the reversed-4-cycle-to-an-empty-rank example. Its second fix ('compute destination offsets by prefix sum and unpack in receive order') is wrong: writes would then land ahead of the read position inside the shared block and overwrite unread records; only a non-overlapping destination area works.
first_pass_critique: Reproduction and analysis correct, and it saw that the review's second fix does not work. Its preferred diff puts a three-line conditional expression inside the memAllocGroup argument list (against his style); it did not add the regression test it itself identified as missing, and its reproducer only used the 'all vertices on rank 0' layout, so it did not establish when the corruption does not show (receiver with its own send data padding the gap), which matters for the test design.

fix_options.label: A: full-size destination edge area when the permutation is user-provided (recommended)
fix_options.summary: dgraphRedist() passes a flag (srcpermgsttax != NULL) to dgraphRedist2(), which sizes the first member of the group as dstedgelocsiz * fledval words in that case (no overlap possible) and keeps the TRICK sizing for the internal, receive-ordered permutation. The final memRealloc already shrinks the block. A second case with a reversed user permutation (all vertices to the last process) is added to test_scotch_dgraph_redist.c.
fix_options.tested: redistperm matrix (np 2-4, three layouts, N 4-41, base 0/1) on 32-bit ASan and 64-bit builds; the new check case fails on pristine and passes patched; After the series: check_strat_par, check_scotch_dgraph_{check,band,coarsen,order,grow,induce,redist}, check_libparmetis_{v3,dual}, check_prog_{dgord,dgpart,dgscat-dggath,dgtst} all exit 0 on the 32-bit ASan+UBSan tree and on the 64-bit Gnum tree ($WORK/chk_32_*.log, chk_64_*.log; the only sanitizer lines are pre-existing ones in library_dgraph_coarsen.c:163 and bgraph_bipart_ml.c:195, other groups); check_scotch_dgraph_{check,coarsen,order,redist,induce} and check_prog_dgord also pass on an ASan -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (chk_dbg_*.log). Zero compiler warnings in the three trees. git am of the 7 patches on a fresh clone of v7.0.17 succeeds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Peak memory of the user-permutation path grows by dstedgelocnbr * fledval words during the exchange (the internal path is unchanged). One more static-function parameter (prototype in dgraph_redist.h).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Keeps his TRICK where it is valid and documents when it is not; dgraphRedist() already branches on 'srcpermgsttax != NULL' ('Do not allocate permutation array if already provided'). Test added in the style of his 2bcd53c edit of the same test file.

fix_options.label: B: always allocate a full-size destination edge area (drop the TRICK)
fix_options.summary: Size the first member as dstedgelocsiz + dstedlolocsiz words in all cases.
fix_options.tested: compiles (mpicc -c, 0 warnings); not run in this pass
fix_options.tradeoffs: Three-line diff, removes a fragile invariant and makes the debug overlap asserts moot, but costs the extra peak memory on the default path too, which is exactly what the TRICK was written to avoid.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He wrote the TRICK deliberately with three comments; he would keep it.

fix_options.summary: The first unpack loop records whether destination indices arrive in increasing order; if not, a separate edge array is allocated and the group block is freed after unpacking.
